question: Which drug class is used as first-line medical therapy for acromegaly when surgery is not curative or is contraindicated, and works by inhibiting GH secretion?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Dopamine agonists are second-line in acromegaly (they work better in prolactinomas). They reduce GH in a minority of acromegaly patients.
Correct! Long-acting somatostatin analogues (octreotide LAR, lanreotide) suppress GH and IGF-1 secretion and are the preferred medical therapy for acromegaly.
Pegvisomant blocks the GH receptor (does not reduce GH levels) and is reserved for patients resistant or intolerant to somatostatin analogues.
GnRH agonists target the reproductive axis, not GH secretion. They are not used to treat acromegaly.

overallFeedback.feedback: Somatostatin analogues (octreotide, lanreotide) mimic endogenous somatostatin, suppressing GH from pituitary somatotroph adenomas. Pegvisomant is reserved for resistance.
Excellent! Somatostatin analogues normalise IGF-1 in ~50–60% of acromegaly patients and are the mainstay of medical management.
